clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms at the end of the Eighty-seventh Congress. Executive Order 10935, signed April 22, 1961 (26 FR 3507, PDF pages 3-3), orders that income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1961, inclusive) returns shall, during the Eighty-seventh Congress, be open to inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives, or any duly authorized subcommittee, for the purpose of carrying on the investigations authorized by clause 18 of Rule XI of the Rules of the House of Representatives, agreed to January 3, 1961. The order sets no other term, condition or revocation clause. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress ended at noon on January 3, 1963 under the Twentieth Amendment, so the grant lapsed no later than that day; recorded as 1963-01-03 inclusive, with the exclusive reading (end when that day begins) disclosed as the alternative. The end source is the order's own operative text. No later amending event is held.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10935 (26 FR 3507, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of April 25, 1961; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10935.txt), headed Executive Order 10935, signed by John F. Kennedy on April 22, 1961. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Inspection of income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order is one grant, a single sentence opening income, excess-profits, estate and gift tax (years 1945 to 1961, inclusive) returns to inspection by the Committee on Un-American Activities, House of Representatives or any duly authorized subcommittee, followed by a sentence fixing its effective date on filing for publication. The grant is limited by its own words to the period of the Eighty-seventh Congress, which I treat as the order's fixed term. The terms of the Members of the Eighty-seventh Congress began at noon on January 3, 1961 and ended at noon on January 3, 1963 (Twentieth Amendment, sections 1 and 2). The Constitution is not among the held texts and no held source states that date, so the end date rests on that constitutional text together with the order's own words; no other source is claimed for it. First end: January 3, 1963 by the order's own terms, recorded inclusive. The exclusive reading (the end when that day begins) is the alternative the owner ruling requires me to disclose, but it fits poorly here because the Congress's terms ran until noon of that day. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, exception or transitional clause; I read its whole text for such wording. Any inspection made while the grant ran is a completed act, and nothing in the order continues the grant after the Eighty-seventh Congress ended. Any later statutory change to the Internal Revenue Code sections the order cites would postdate this end and cannot be a first end.
